national_raw_news.content: BRICS nations have unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration on the First day of the BRICS Summit 2026, being held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed to adopt the declaration at the end of the session on the first day of the summit. In his closing remarks, the Prime Minister noted that the New Delhi Declaration adopted today provides a clear direction for the shared resolve of the member countries. He added that it is now their shared responsibility to translate these resolutions into tangible results. The Prime Minister said that today’s discussion makes it evident that the changing world cannot be steered by outdated institutions and underlined that reforms are essential in representation, responsiveness, and rule-making. Mr Modi said that the leaders also emphasised that the Global South must have equal participation in the development of future technologies and the rules governing them. He emphasised that the gap between decisions and their outcomes must be bridged through partnership and collective action. The Prime Minister also expressed his gratitude to the leaders for their valuable contributions, constructive spirit and commitment as the BRICS Chair. To mark the 20 years of BRICS, two commemorative postage stamps were also released by the leaders of the member countries on this occasion. Earlier in his opening remarks on the first day of the session, which was based on inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism, Mr Modi proposed a BRICS Continuity and Implementation Mechanism to ensure that the grouping’s institutional momentum is maintained despite the Chairship changing every year. In his opening remarks at today’s session of the BRICS Summit 2026, which is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Mr Modi said the mechanism would enable follow-up of all initiatives and outcomes through the Troika. The Prime Minister said BRICS countries will have to work on a new and ambitious agenda for the next 20 years. He said the process must begin with the grouping’s own working system. The Prime Minister also proposed to establish a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect the maritime authorities and diplomatic missions of relevant countries to facilitate assistance during difficult times. Mr Modi observed that seafarers make a massive contribution to global trade, yet they often find themselves lacking support during difficult times. Mr Modi said the time has come to translate the unity and consensus among BRICS countries into concrete outcomes on the global stage. He stressed that BRICS members respect one another and move forward through consensus. He said the grouping is not working against anyone, but is moving forward with the approach of taking everyone along. The Prime Minister described this year’s BRICS Summit as a historic milestone, noting that the grouping is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year. He said BRICS is at its coming-of-age moment and has established its distinct identity on the global stage over the past two decades. Mr Modi said India’s Chairship of BRICS is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. He said Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability have been India’s foremost priorities as Chair. Guided by these priorities, India has laid special emphasis on connecting BRICS cooperation directly with the common people. The Prime Minister noted that with this vision, more than 350 meetings were organised, and India had the privilege of welcoming delegations across nearly 30 cities in the country. In his address, the Prime Minister noted that the Global South stands in the front row of global crises but in the back row of decision-making. He emphasised transforming this ‘pyramid of privilege’ into a ‘platform of partnership’. In this context, the Prime Minister proposed to jointly formulate 10 proposals for global governance reform, aiming to shape them into a BRICS reform roadmap by the time of the next Summit. On the issue of reform in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), the Prime Minister emphasised that reform of the UNSC can no longer be postponed and negotiations on this matter must be linked to a definite time frame and clear outcomes. He said, similarly, voting power, leadership positions, and policy priorities within financial institutions must align with today’s economic realities. A 13 member delegation comprising journalists from Srinagar along with PIB officials will take part in the tour. Ahead of the delegation’s departure, Director PIB Srinagar, Qazi Salman, briefed the participants on the objectives of the visit, urging them to make meaningful use of the interactions and interviews planned during their time in Chennai. The delegation is being led by Shahid Lone, Field Publicity Officer at CBC Anantnag, who will serve as Conducting Officer for the tour, with Ifham Ul Islam, Information Assistant at PIB Srinagar, also accompanying the group. The tour is designed to give the visiting journalists firsthand exposure to key Central Government institutions, projects and initiatives based in Chennai, with the aim of deepening their understanding of national level policies and how these are implemented on the ground in different parts of the country. During the visit, the delegation will tour various Central Government establishments and projects in the city and interact with senior officials to better understand their functioning and day to day operations. Addressing the delegation before departure, Qazi Salman congratulated the participants and expressed confidence that the visit would offer valuable opportunities for professional engagement and a better understanding of how Central Government institutions function beyond what journalists typically encounter in their regular regional coverage. national_raw_news.content: J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects - https://onlykashmir.in/ Facebook Instagram Pinterest X Website Youtube State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Only Kashmir Behind The News Facebook Instagram X Only Kashmir Behind The News State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Home Spotlight Spotlight State J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects By Online Editor September 12, 2026 Advertisement Mirwaiz Umar Farooq meets Iranian President and Foreign Minister in New Delhi September 13, 2026 J&K Filmmakers Win Big at IFFJK 2026 September 12, 2026 PIB Srinagar Takes Journalists on Chennai Tour September 12, 2026 J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects September 12, 2026 PM Modi Pitches Key BRICS Initiatives September 12, 2026 Advertisement - Advertisement - Onlykashmir.in News Desk The Jammu and Kashmir Government, led by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, has accorded administrative approval for two major parking infrastructure projects in Jammu city at a combined estimated cost of ₹49.34 crore, a move aimed at easing the persistent traffic congestion that has become a familiar challenge in the winter capital’s busier commercial areas. The approved projects include a Parking-cum-Commercial Complex at Parade and a Multilevel Car Parking facility at SMGS Hospital, two locations that have long struggled with inadequate parking capacity relative to the volume of vehicular traffic and footfall they see on a daily basis. Officials said the projects are intended to provide modern, organised parking facilities at these key locations, easing congestion and improving overall traffic management in the city. The new facilities are also expected to promote better utilisation of available urban space and support planned, sustainable urban development, an approach the government has increasingly emphasised as Jammu continues to grow and its existing infrastructure comes under greater strain. Officials added that the parking infrastructure will offer greater convenience to commuters, visitors and residents alike, particularly in areas that routinely witness heavy vehicular movement and acute parking pressure during peak hours.
